page_placements.theme: Shares of interpretable or polysemantic units outside language models (vision CNNs, ViT/CLIP, audio, tabular, CT encoders)

record.file_problem: The main text is readable and complete. Some appendix pages have garbled text, but this does not prevent extracting the main results.
record.tranche_reason: The study applies compositional neuron explanations to vision and NLI models and reports results about neuron concepts and explanation fit in those settings.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own neuron audit and IoU results. It does not test explanations on a held-out set of activations or report the Qwen3 pole-share categories in the claim. Its copy-paste attacks are not included because they do not test a listed version’s specific outcome.
record.test_reason: No listed version is tested. The study audits neurons in a Places365 ResNet-18 and an SNLI BiLSTM-MLP using compositional explanations (beam search over Broden or lexical concepts, scored by IoU). It never studies Qwen3 or other large language models (V1, V2), InceptionV1's cat/car neurons or recursive generalization (V3), attribution graphs (V5), held-out activation prediction (V6), or simulation-based scoring (V7). It also never compares the share of interpretable neurons across tools or architectures (V4). Its 69%/31% meaningful/polysemantic split and its low mean IoU are related findings on neuron interpretability in other settings, so they go under fits_no_version. The reader's 'tests'/T3 contradicts its own finding that every version is not_tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that compositional explanations characterize neurons better than atomic labels and reveal abstractions and polysemanticity in vision, plus shallow lexical heuristics in NLI. In vision, interpretability correlates positively with accuracy when the neuron fires (r=0.31); in NLI the correlation is negative (r=-0.60). The explanations also enable copy-paste adversarial examples. The authors caution that neuron-level explanations miss distributed concepts and do not establish causal chains.
record.recipe_differences: The study searches compositions of annotated concepts using beam search and IoU, rather than auditing poles with the claim’s method.
record.method_sensitivity: In vision, mean IoU increases with maximum formula length, from 0.059 at length 1 to 0.099 at length 10. In NLI, the reported IoU trend continues increasing past length 30.

fits_no_version.finding: In a random sample of 128 ResNet-18 (Places365) final-layer units, manual inspection judged 69% meaningful compositional abstractions and 31% polysemantic, firing for at least some unrelated concepts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In a mid-size vision CNN, even with richer compositional explanation tools, roughly a third of late-layer neurons look polysemantic by inspection.

fits_no_version.finding: Mean IoU between neuron masks and the best explanations rises only from 0.059 (length 1) to 0.099 (length 10). The authors note considerable unexplained behavior; NLI IoU keeps rising past length 30.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Neurons judged meaningful by inspection are matched only loosely by their best explanations across the full probe set, so a 'meaningful' label overstates how much of a neuron's firing is explained.

record.problems: The manual interpretability audit covers only 128 vision neurons. The authors note that annotations may omit relevant concepts, and that neuron-level explanations cannot capture all concepts or establish causal chains. Explanation IoU is measured on the probing data used to construct explanations, not on held-out activations.
record.rows_left_out: Copy-paste adversarial examples in Sections 6 and Figures 8–9 were omitted because they do not measure any listed version’s specified outcome. Additional example explanations in Appendices C–D were also omitted; they are illustrative rather than separate measurements of the listed versions.

untested.parts: Whole version: no Qwen3-32B audit and no pole shares.
Whole version: no share estimates for language models, dense or mixture-of-experts, at any scale. The NLI model is a small BiLSTM and no share is reported for it.
Whole version: no InceptionV1 cat/car analysis and no test of recursive generalization versus superposition.
No comparison of interpretable-neuron shares across tools or architectures. The study shows IoU and concept uniqueness rise with formula length, but reports no share under the length-1 tool.
Whole version: no attribution graphs and no reconstruction-error comparison.
No held-out prediction test of explanations derived from activating examples.
No activation-simulation scoring on new text.

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. The copy-paste attacks, the accuracy correlations and the concept-uniqueness tables (A.1–A.2) were rightly left out as bearing on no version. The NetDissect-to-compositional relabeling (e.g. the 'bullring' unit actually detects sports fields) is suggestive for V4's point about tools, but gives no shares.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not audit Qwen3-32B or report shares for poles with one job, two related jobs, or not-yet-understood poles.
It does not report comparable job-share estimates across language models, dense and mixture-of-experts models, or model scales up to trillions of parameters.
It does not analyze InceptionV1 cat-and-car neurons or recursive generalization.
It does not test the proposed causes of messy neurons or compare interpretability estimates across architectures and tools.
It does not build attribution graphs or measure their behavioral explanation or reconstruction error.
The study does not evaluate explanations on activations held out from explanation generation.
It does not simulate neuron activations on new text or report automated explanation scores on such text.

rows.operation_detail: Manual inspection and categorization of length-10 explanations for a random sample of 128 neurons
rows.value: 69% learned a meaningful combination of concepts; 31% were polysemantic. Of the 88 meaningful neurons, 50 (57%) were lexically and perceptually coherent abstractions, 28 (32%) were perceptual abstractions without lexical coherence, and 10 (12%) showed specialization.
rows.note: The paper describes the 31% as firing for at least some unrelated concepts. This is not the Qwen3 pole categorization in the claim.

relation.reason: It studies neuron interpretability and polysemanticity in other models and does not test a version. 'tests' would be too strong.

tranche.reason: The study audits Places365 ResNet-18 and SNLI BiLSTM units with its own method (beam search, IoU). It reports no result on any listed version: not the Qwen3 pole audit, other LLMs, InceptionV1 cat/car, a tools-vs-share comparison, circuits or simulation scoring. The reader's T3 is too generous.

source_check.notes: The 69%/31% split is a manual judgment on 128 units of one vision model, using explanations from a compositional-IoU method. It is not comparable to the Qwen3 pole shares in V1. The paper gives no interpretable share under atomic (NetDissect) labels, so it does not test V4's tools claim. It reports only that mean IoU rises from 0.059 to 0.099. No verdicts are listed, and none are warranted.

statements.correction: Of 128 randomly sampled ResNet-18 (Places365) final-layer units, manual inspection of length-10 explanations: 69% learned some meaningful combination of concepts (88 units: 57% lexically coherent abstraction, 32% perceptual-only abstraction, 12% specialization); 31% polysemantic (fire for at least some unrelated concepts).
statements.problem: Numbers match the text (128 random units, length-10 explanations, 69% meaningful, 31% polysemantic). Minor wording point: 10 of the 88 meaningful units (12%) are 'specialization' (L1 AND NOT L2) rather than abstractions, but the text's own phrase is 'meaningful combination of concepts', so 'meaningful compositional' is a fair reading.
